title: Opaque stream handle for resumable reads, timeouts, and cancellation
creator: Aisha Patel
comments: 2026-03-10 — Kickoff: scoped the work with PM and DX; agreed on StreamHandle as the primary abstraction. Action: prototype an API in go-sdk and verify no regressions in examples.
2026-03-11 — Design review: showed prototype to runtime and serving teams. Main feedback: ensure backoff is configurable per-handle and surface metrics for reconnects and timeouts.

2026-03-12 — Engineering note: Implemented prototype where Recv() spawns an internal goroutine that reads the transport and sends messages over a buffered chan; cancellation closes transports and the chan to avoid goroutine leaks. Need to document caveats around long-running RecvWithTimeout loops.

2026-03-13 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/462 — adds StreamHandle, RecvWithTimeout, Resume(), and observability hooks. Unit tests for cancellation races in pack run. Asking for review from @lena-ortiz and @samir-choi.

2026-03-14 — Addressed review: replaced busy-wait reconnect with jittered exponential backoff, added metrics (stream.reconnect.count, stream.timeout.count). Updated examples in docs/streaming.md. Next: integration test against staging runtime with simulated transport drops.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes StreamHandle with Recv, RecvWithTimeout, Resume, and Close methods
Canceling the parent context cancels the logical stream and releases all goroutines within 100ms in unit tests
RecvWithTimeout does not cancel the logical stream when it times out (returns a documented timeout error instead)
Resume succeeds on server-supported stream tokens and emits a metric and event for each reconnect attempt
Automated race detection (go test -race) shows no leaks in the new streaming unit tests
Documentation and one-short-example added to go-sdk README and console examples
design_decision: We chose an opaque StreamHandle that separates logical request lifetime from per-read operations. Alternatives considered: (A) leave semantics as-is and add helper wrappers (rejected: too fragile for complex apps), (B) force per-read contexts to propagate to the transport and cancel on timeout (rejected: caused unintended stream termination), (C) adopt per-handle reconnect state with server-side resume tokens (chosen). The chosen approach gives predictable behavior for app developers, supports resume where the server provides tokens, and keeps surface area small.
testing_plan: Unit tests for RecvWithTimeout returning ErrTimeout without cancelling handle
Race test suite focusing on simultaneous Cancel, Resume, and Recv ops
Integration test in staging injecting NACKs and simulated TCP resets to validate Resume/backoff behavior
Load test with 500 concurrent stream handles to surface resource usage and verify metrics under stress
Fuzz around payload ordering to ensure Resume does not duplicate visible outputs when server provides sequence tokens
rollout_plan: Merge feature on canary branch behind feature flag (go-sdk: streaming_handle=true)
Enable for internal customers and Redwood integrations team for 2 weeks
Monitor metrics: stream.reconnect.count, stream.timeout.count, stream.goroutine_leaks (via runtime.NumGoroutine sampling)
Gradual ramp to GA after no regressions and signoff from runtime and DX teams
